title: Researcher says an ice-rock fall off Langtang Lirung, not a lake burst, may have caused the flood
body: Santosh Nepal, a water resources and climate change researcher, told Onlinekhabar on Friday that the flood may have started with a huge ice and rock fall off Langtang Lirung rather than a glacial lake bursting, which was the earlier working theory.

He said satellite images show a mass of ice, snow and rock falling from about 5,000 to 5,500 metres on the mountain's northern slope and dropping nearly 2,000 metres into the Lhende Khola. The impact could have released enough energy to melt snow and ice fast enough to send a sudden surge of water downstream, without a lake first forming and bursting.

Nepal said the mechanism looks similar to Uttarakhand's 2021 Chamoli disaster, and that it is too early to conclude what happened. He said researchers still need more satellite data and a field investigation once conditions allow.
This is one researcher's preliminary reading, not a finding from the government or ICIMOD, and the cause of the flood is still not officially confirmed.
